defectus

radix/corpus/defectus/defectus.fab (canonical · operator)#

Supplies a default value when a failable call fails: f(x) ⊥ v.

# =============================================================================
# defectus — Supplies a default value when a failable call fails: f(x) ⊥ v.
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Call default — `f(x) ⊥ v` gives `v` when `f` fails through its `⇥` channel, and the call's value otherwise.
#   • Lazy default — `v` is evaluated only when the call fails.
#   • Propagation versus default — inside a `⇥` function a bare failable call propagates; `⊥` handles the failure at the call site instead.
#   • Traps are not caught — `⊥` catches only the `⇥` channel, never `انهر` or runtime traps.
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Using `⊥` on a call that cannot fail — only a call whose signature has `⇥` takes a default.
#   • Writing both — `f(x) ⊥ 0 ⇥ E` is rejected: one expression propagates or defaults, never both.
#
# See also: ⊥, ⇥, ارم, فخ, انهر
# =============================================================================

# defectus — the call-site default channel (D17.7)
#
# GRAMMAR:
#   callDefault :← call '⊥' unary
#
# EXPECTED OUTPUT:
#   4 -1
#   fallback
#   2 -1
#   2 -1
#   2 -1
#
# BACKEND:
#   Desugars through the `فخ` trap machinery; Go and TypeScript fail
#   closed until they emit `فخ`.

fn half(int n) → int ⇥ string {
    if n % 2 ≠ 0 {
        throw "odd"
    }
    return n / 2
}

fn fallback() → int {
    print "fallback"
    return -1
}

# Propagation: a bare failable call inside a `⇥` function sends the failure
# on to this function's caller.
fn quarter(int n) → int ⇥ string {
    return half(half(n))
}

# `⊥` also handles a propagated failure at the outer call site.
fn safeQuarter(int n) → int {
    return quarter(n) ⊥ -1
}

fn fatal(int n) → int ⇥ string {
    if n ≡ 0 {
        panic "fatal"
    }
    return n
}

main {
    # The call's value on success, the default on failure.
    const int a ← half(8) ⊥ 0
    const int b ← half(7) ⊥ -1
    print a, b

    # The default runs only when the call fails: `fallback` prints once.
    const int c ← half(4) ⊥ fallback()
    const int d ← half(5) ⊥ fallback()
    print c, d

    print safeQuarter(8), safeQuarter(6)

    # `⊥` never catches `panic`; this would still abort:
    # const int e ← fatal(0) ⊥ 1
    print fatal(2) ⊥ 0, half(1) ⊥ -1
}

Expected output:

4 -1
fallback
2 -1
2 -1
2 -1
